column1: # MSL 9.0.3 members the exe links, by the exe VA of the member's first matched function.
# Derived 2026-10-06 (lane QBM) by masked byte search of every code section of MSL_All_x86.lib
# members in the exe's .text above 0x004d3000. tools/pullorder.py pulls each from
# MSL_All_x86.lib at its VA (Research/the-link-step.md). Corrected against
# vendor/msl/linked.tsv (lanes QBV, QBQ): setupargs, mbstring and buffer_io start one function
# earlier; ExceptionX86's first function is 0x00534930 (0x00534890 is excrtl's static
# initializer), so it follows exchand as in the exe. strtold.obj has no function in the exe
# (0x00506ec0 is alloc.obj's malloc) but its 24-byte table is the exe's .data at 0x0057cac0,
# right before ansifp_x86's: it is pulled there, at ansifp_x86's VA and listed before it.
# NewHand.obj is out: no function and none of its data in the exe (0x0054dc60 and 0x0054dc80
# Members with no live code, placed by their .bss and .data (lane QCD): float.obj's ___float_nan and
# ___float_huge are the exe's .data at 0x0057cab4, just before strtold.obj's table; the exe's .bss holds
# stdio_posix.win32.obj (768) and unistd.win32.obj (264) as the 1,032 bytes at 0x0086ce28 after
# extras.obj (lane QDA): the exe's StrCaseCmp at 0x004ff950 is its _stricmp (linked from the library
# since lane RS, 2026-10-13; burgerstrcase.c is gone), so the member is pulled there and its 768-byte .bss sits
# between atplatheap's and direct_io.obj's blocks, where the exe's .bss has the hole; it was pulled last.
